 Hanes: A sense of duty awakens beyond Remembrance Day 
 With international headwinds now blowing, attitudes toward military service are shifting. 
 A member of the Grenadier Guards stands as part of the honour guard at the cenotaph on Remembrance Day in Montreal in 2024. (Allen McInnis / Montreal Gazette) 
 By 
 Allison Hanes 
 November 11, 2026 at 6:00 a.m. 
 According to family lore, my paternal grandfather lied about his age and signed up to serve in the First World War when he was just 17.
 Whether in search of adventure in the Great War or escape from a hardscrabble life, what the teenage farmboy encountered haunted him for the rest of his days.
 Like many ex-soldiers, my grandfather hardly talked about what he endured in the rat-infested trenches or saw on the blood-soaked battlefields of Europe. But we know he fought at Vimy Ridge and survived a mustard gas attack — which later helped send him to an early grave.
